::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Reminder, 2026-09-30.** Nothing is built. The purpose in Section 1 is a first
guess, and Section 5 lists the questions that have to be answered before
choosing a tool.
:::

## 1. Goal

Set up a second brain: one place holding the documents, notes and code
accumulated over the years, searchable by an AI assistant that can answer a
question from them and say which document the answer came from.

The first guess at the purpose has two parts.

- **Find past work.** A question such as "where did I work out the EC50
  identifiability argument?" should return the document, not a search of four
  places by hand.
- **Keep learning.** Feeding the store and querying it is itself practice with
  the tools, and the store makes connections between old and new projects
  visible.

## 2. Out of Scope

- **Not published.** The store holds private material. Nothing from Google
  Drive is copied into this repository, and this page describes the plan only.
- **Not [Collected Wisdom](../collected-wisdom/index.qmd).** That project indexes
  the personal Google Docs on meaning, parenting and music as a site. This one
  is a private search tool over everything, work material included. The Google
  Drive inventory in Section 3 can serve both.

## 3. Sources

| # | Source | What it holds | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Google Drive | Documents, slides and spreadsheets from years of work | Have an agent scour it and propose what is useful before loading anything |
| 2 | TrinityMetrics | Every project, blog post and guide on this site | Already in git and in Markdown, so the easiest source to load |
| 3 | Other GitHub repositories | `synpmx`, `xgxr` and the rest | Code and vignettes |
| 4 | Papers | The PDFs and reference manager library behind the literature reviews | |
| 5 | Email and meeting notes | Decisions and the reasons for them | Most sensitive; decide last |
| 6 | Claude conversations | Sessions that worked something out and were never written up | Check what can be exported |
| 7 | Bookmarks and read-later lists | Things meant to be read | |

Rows 1 and 2 come first. The rest wait until the purpose in Section 5 is
settled, since each one widens what has to be kept private.

For Google Drive, the first pass is an inventory rather than a load: a list of
folders and documents, a sentence on each, and a mark for keep, skip or
private. An agent with read access to Drive can draft it; Andy decides the
marks.

## 4. Candidate Tools

A second brain in this sense is two parts: a store of documents, and a
retrieval step that finds the passages relevant to a question and hands them to
a language model to answer from. The second part is called retrieval-augmented
generation (RAG). The tools below differ in where the store lives and who runs
the retrieval.

| Tool | Store | Fits |
|---|---|---|
| NotebookLM | Google, reads Drive directly | Google Drive with no copying; limits on source count per notebook |
| Claude Projects | Uploaded files in claude.ai | A few dozen documents per project |
| A folder of Markdown files, queried by Claude Code | Local disk, in git | TrinityMetrics and other repositories as they already are |
| Obsidian | Local Markdown with links between notes | Writing new notes as well as searching old ones |

None has been tried for this yet. The term "second brain" comes from Tiago
Forte's *Building a Second Brain* (2022), which is about organizing notes by
hand; the AI retrieval step is the newer part.

## 5. Open Questions

1. **What question should the store answer that cannot be answered now?** Two
   or three real examples decide the tool better than a feature list.
2. **Work and personal together, or apart?** Work material may have rules on
   where it can be uploaded.
3. **Load a copy, or point at the original?** A copy goes stale; a pointer
   depends on the tool reading Drive or git directly.
4. **Who adds to it, and when?** A store that is loaded once and never updated
   stops being useful within a year.

## 6. First Steps

1. Write down three questions the second brain should be able to answer.
2. Have an agent inventory Google Drive, as in Section 3.
3. Try NotebookLM on a handful of Drive documents and Claude Code on
   TrinityMetrics, and compare the answers to the three questions.
